description:
You are a site reliability engineer tasked with monitoring server uptime from a log file. There is a file located at /home/user/uptime_log.txt. Each line in this file contains three columns separated by spaces: timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS), hostname, and uptime_seconds. Your goal is to produce a report with only the hostname and uptime_seconds columns (columns 2 and 3), and save the output in a new file called /home/user/uptime_report.txt. The columns in the new file must be separated by a single space, and there must be no trailing spaces at the end of each line. The output should retain the original order from the log file. For example, the contents of /home/user/uptime_report.txt should look like: 
server01 12233
server02 9940
server03 5831
Please ensure that the report is generated accurately using terminal column manipulation commands. Do not manually edit files—use command-line tools. After you are finished, the /home/user/uptime_report.txt file should exist and contain only the specified columns from every line in the source log.
truth:
Before the agent starts, the file /home/user/uptime_log.txt exists with the following contents: 
2024-05-27 14:01:20 server01 12233
2024-05-27 14:01:27 server02 9940
2024-05-27 14:01:36 server03 5831
After correct completion, /home/user/uptime_report.txt is created with the following exact contents (no leading/trailing whitespace, columns separated by a single space, each line terminated by a newline): 
server01 12233
server02 9940
server03 5831
name: task_000000_af041421
